title: Who Are You Becoming?
headline: Who Are You Becoming? The Battle Is Bigger Than the Thought
tagline: You can be growing in things people celebrate while shrinking in things heaven values.
seo_title: Who Are You Becoming? Character, Thoughts and Formation | TheWrkShop
seo_description: You can accomplish something impressive while becoming someone you never intended to be. A devotional for men on 2 Corinthians 10:5 and 3:18.
verse_text: We demolish arguments and every pretension that sets itself up against the knowledge of God, and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.

scriptures.text: We demolish arguments and every pretension that sets itself up against the knowledge of God, and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
For those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son….
And we all…. contemplating the Lord’s glory, are being transformed into his image with ever-increasing glory….

items: For much of our lives, we have been trained to evaluate ourselves by what we do.
What did I accomplish?
What did I build?
What did I earn?
What goals did I achieve?
Those questions matter.
But Scripture asks something deeper.
It is possible to accomplish something impressive while becoming someone you never intended to become.
You can build the business and become consumed by it.
You can win the argument and become increasingly proud.
You can protect yourself from being hurt and become increasingly hardened.
You can become knowledgeable about Scripture and increasingly uncorrectable.
Success by itself cannot tell you whether you are being formed well.
You can be growing in things people celebrate while shrinking in things heaven values.
You are becoming someone.
Right now.
In ordinary moments nobody else notices.

sections.label: The Battle Is Bigger Than the Thought

items: Why do thoughts matter so much?
Because thoughts do not always remain isolated thoughts.
A thought can receive attention.
Attention can influence interpretation.
Interpretation can become agreement.
Agreement can strengthen belief.
Belief can influence desire and decisions.
Decisions can become habits.
Habits can shape character.
And character influences the direction of a life.
Not mechanically.
Not every passing thought becomes character.
And none of this means we transform ourselves apart from God’s grace.
But it does mean: moments matter.
No accomplishment is worth becoming someone Christ never called you to become.
Don’t only ask, “Did I get there?” Ask, “Who did I become while getting there?”
Character rarely appears suddenly. It is often revealed suddenly.
The goal isn’t perfection. The goal is increasing responsiveness to Christ.
Capture the thought before the thought participates in capturing your direction.
